oil.when: 2017 with the steering-wheel arrow and OK buttons
steps: Reset only after the oil and filter have actually been changed.
Turn the ignition on and open the main menu in the instrument cluster with the steering-wheel arrow buttons.
Scroll to Settings and press the right arrow, then scroll to Convenience and press the right arrow again.
Scroll to Oil Life Reset and press and hold OK until the cluster shows Reset Successful.
Check that oil life now reads 100%. If it shows Not Reset or Reset Cancelled, go through the steps again.
oil.note: The manual shows three cluster menu layouts for this year. If Oil Life Reset is not under Convenience on your truck, look for it elsewhere in the Settings menu.

tpms.when: 2017: light clears after a short drive; after every tire rotation, retrain the sensors with the hazard-flasher method
steps: Set all four tires to the cold pressures on the driver's door jamb sticker (front and rear can differ).
If you only added air, drive above 20 mph for at least two minutes. The light should go out by itself.
After a tire rotation, drive above 20 mph for at least two minutes, then park safely where you can reach every tire with an air hose.
Turn the ignition off, then back on without starting the engine (key left in).
Within 10 seconds, turn the hazard flashers on and off three times. The horn sounds once and the tire pressure light flashes.
Start at the left front tire: take off the valve cap and let air out slowly until the horn sounds once.
Repeat on the right front, then the right rear, then the left rear. Do not wait more than two minutes between tires.
After the last tire the light stops flashing. Turn the ignition off and set all tires back to the door-sticker pressures.
If the horn sounds twice at any point, the reset did not take. Start the whole procedure again.
tpms.note: If the light flashes for about a minute every time you start the truck and then stays on, the system has a fault that adding air or this reset will not clear; have it checked. The light also stays on while the spare is in use. On dual-rear-wheel trucks the sequence also includes the inner and outer rear tires; follow the order in the owner's manual or have a tire shop do it.

notes: The 2017 Super Duty owner's manual covers the F-250, F-350, F-450 and F-550, so the F-350 uses these same steps. The manual calls for the hazard-flasher sensor reset after every tire rotation.
